verifiedProduct.improvement: process health readiness terminates immediately on authoritative child terminal state, aborts in-flight health requests on child exit, and reports real exit/spawn details
implementation: observe spawn/error/close once through a terminal lifecycle state
wait for successful spawn before process-start evidence
race health requests and retry waits against terminal state
abort hanging fetch when process terminates
record spawn failures as structured process-error evidence without false process-start
preserved: all supported targets and acceptance gates

runtime: hanging health request cancelled on child exit

ecosystemRotation: process supervision; readiness/health polling; service lifecycle; subprocess errors; service testing/orchestration

candidates.head: e2b33e220f047a85c25d0e579b747cc7663821c1
candidates.architecture: native libuv/process primitives with evented ChildProcess API
candidates.harvest: spawn=successful launch; error=failure; close=authoritative process+stdio terminal state; avoid double-handling
candidates.benefit: faster and more accurate Ferrum process failure attribution without a dependency
candidates.risks: event ordering can duplicate handling if error and exit/close are treated independently
candidates.issues: official docs warn consumers listening to error plus exit must guard duplicate callbacks
candidates.evidence: primary Node ChildProcess event contract and current source
candidates.experiment: spawn failure, early exit, signal exit and late stdio close under Ferrum
candidates.acceptance: single terminal result, no unhandled error, no false process-start, full logs preserved

candidates.architecture: single binary with dependencies, readiness/liveness, recovery, CLI/TUI/API/MCP
candidates.harvest: newer stop/terminal intent supersedes stale restart, dependency, and readiness work
candidates.benefit: avoid waits/restarts continuing after authoritative lifecycle changes
candidates.risks: multi-process semantics are broader than Ferrum current target contract
candidates.issues: recent fixes prevent restart-in-flight overriding stop and abort dependency waits on termination
candidates.experiment: model Ferrum process terminal/readiness races with identical workloads
candidates.acceptance: terminal intent cancels stale waits without target/evidence loss
candidates.review: upstream lifecycle changes or Ferrum multi-process reproducer

challenge.reason: Execa, PM2, Supervisor and concurrently did not demonstrate a same-workload Ferrum advantage worth replacing the small native runner. Testcontainers and Toxiproxy require a real disposable service fixture before adoption can be judged.
nextExperiments: prototype a disposable real API/service fixture behind Ferrum's stable lifecycle/evidence contract using Testcontainers Node or the smallest equivalent Docker-managed adapter
after the service fixture exists, compare deterministic latency/reset/timeout recovery using Toxiproxy while preserving native raw evidence
only if a real persistent-service use case appears, evaluate distinct startup/readiness/liveness semantics inspired by Kubernetes/systemd

nextResearchCursor: disposable service/API fixtures and lifecycle adapters
service network fault injection and recovery
multi-process/dependency orchestration only when a concrete target requires it
guardrails: No reduced target coverage, skipped runtime proof, reduced polling/check frequency, reduced evidence, stale caching, caps, or weaker tests.
Process/service integrations remain additive until same-workload real-runtime parity and measurable benefit are proven.
Do not replace Ferrum's direct browser/extension/mobile/desktop evidence paths with service orchestration abstractions.
